# An integer-base mixed centroid can have depth below one third

This is a counterexample to the exploratory bound 1/3 for an actual mixed
centroid when n=1. It does not violate OC, whose constant here is 2/9.

Let

    T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)},
    A=T intersect {x<=2/9}
      =conv{(0,0),(2/9,0),(2/9,7/9),(0,1)},
    C=conv[({-1} x A) union ({0} x T) union ({1} x A)].

This is a bounded full-dimensional convex body in R x R^2. Its only
integer fibers are A,T,A. The endpoint fibers are exact by extremality of
their base indices. The middle fiber is exact because (A+A)/2=A subset T;
every convex combination at base 0 is a mixture of A and T. All three
fibers have positive area, so the relevant measure is H_2.

Put c=area(T)=1/2. Elementary integrations in x give

    area(A)/c=2 integral_0^(2/9)(1-x)dx=32/81,
    (1/c) integral_A x dxdy=2 integral_0^(2/9)x(1-x)dx
                           =92/2187,
    (1/c) integral_A y dxdy=integral_0^(2/9)(1-x)^2 dx
                           =386/2187.

The total mixed area is M=c(1+64/81)=c(145/81). The base centroid is
exactly 0 because the endpoint areas agree. Its continuous coordinates are

    g_x=[1/3+2(92/2187)]/(145/81)=913/3915,
    g_y=[1/3+2(386/2187)]/(145/81)=1501/3915.

The point (0,g_x,g_y) belongs to the middle triangle, since both
coordinates are positive and their sum is 2414/3915<1.

The closed ambient cap

    H={x>=913/3915}

contains the centroid on its boundary. Since

    913/3915 - 2/9 =43/3915>0,

it excludes both endpoint fibers. Its cut in T is a similar triangle of
area c(1-g_x)^2. Therefore

    H_2(S intersect H)/H_2(S)
      =(3002/3915)^2/(145/81)
      =9012004/27437625
      <1/3.

The strict comparison is the integer inequality
27036012<27437625. The ratio is approximately 0.32845, which remains above
the required OC constant 2/9. No claim about the maximum depth of S is
made; the point being tested is precisely the actual mixed centroid.

## The same mechanism in arbitrary continuous dimension

Let T be the standard d-simplex, normalized in calculations by its volume,
and let A_a=T intersect {x_1<=a}, where 0<a<1. Use fibers A_a,T,A_a at
-1,0,1. Their endpoint mass ratio is

    r=1-(1-a)^d,

and their endpoint x_1 moment divided by vol(T) is

    m=[1-(d+1)(1-a)^d+d(1-a)^(d+1)]/(d+1).

The actual centroid's first continuous coordinate is

    t=[1/(d+1)+2m]/(1+2r).

There is a unique b in (d/(d+1),1) solving

    2 b^(d+1)-3(d+1)b+3d=0.

The defining polynomial is positive at d/(d+1), negative at 1, and has
negative derivative on this interval. Taking a=1-b gives exactly t=a.
The cap x_1>=a then has zero endpoint d-volume and normalized mass

    b^d/(3-2b^d).

This formula records an exact family, not a minimization theorem for the
family or for all mixed bodies. In d=1 it gives (sqrt(3)-1)/2. In d=2 the
rational choice a=2/9 above avoids algebraic parameters and already
certifies a value below 1/3.
